author: Claude, from the Whisper transcripts and extracted video frames, before any Phase 6 retrieval was built
about: Golden QA set (ROADMAP Phase 6). `windows` are [start_s, end_s] spans where the answer is said or shown; a retrieved passage or citation counts as a hit if it overlaps a window. Types: factual (one specific answer), broad (summary-style, judged on the answer only), visual (answer only on screen, never spoken), unanswerable (the talk doesn't cover it: the correct behaviour is to say so).

questions.question: How long ago did Blender become open source, and where?
questions.answer: 20 years ago, in Amsterdam.

questions.question: What did the doctors tell the speaker about his health?
questions.answer: They declared him fully clean; he doesn't have to worry and is as healthy as he can be.

questions.question: Why wasn't Blender part of the metaverse events at SIGGRAPH?
questions.answer: The organizers forgot to invite Blender; the speaker also felt Blender is small and wouldn't belong among corporations with billion-dollar budgets.

questions.question: What new initiative was announced for the future of Blender?
questions.answer: Blender Lab: a group of five to ten top people working on Blender's future, such as AR/VR, networking and online collaboration.

questions.question: What are the three freedoms behind 'the freedom to create'?
questions.answer: Open-source software, access to creative resources and production knowledge, and access to markets.

questions.question: What are Blender apps?
questions.answer: Blend files packaged with Python-driven UI as custom applications, such as a video player, review tool or 3D-printing tool, that can be shared or given to clients.

questions.question: What happened to the Blender Studio feature film project?
questions.answer: It was dropped: a production company took over the rights and may develop it further.

questions.question: Which studio was shut down right when its series was ready, and by whom?
questions.answer: Tencent Animation, a studio of 300-400 people working in Blender; Netflix pulled the plug.

questions.question: What license must Blender add-ons use, and what platform is planned for them?
questions.answer: GPL; an official extensions platform with pre-approved, high-quality add-ons, run with the community.

questions.question: What is the main message of this keynote?
questions.answer: Blender, as a community-driven open-source project without shareholders, should help shape the future (the 3D internet, AI tools) in artists' interests: freedom to create, open source, and empowering individuals and small teams rather than big corporations or Hollywood pipelines.

questions.question: Which GPU does the speaker recommend for rendering in Blender?
questions.answer: Not covered.

questions.question: When will Blender 4.0 be released?
questions.answer: Not covered.

questions.question: Why did the architect of the Berlin train station sue, and what did the court order?
questions.answer: Deutsche Bahn replaced his vaulted ceiling design with a cheaper flat ceiling; the court found his design defaced and ordered the ceiling rebuilt (reportedly 30 million euros).

questions.question: What did the shopping mall do to Michael Snow's sculpture of geese?
questions.answer: At Christmas 1982 it hung red ribbons around the geese's necks; the court ordered them removed.

questions.question: Which philosophers is personality theory associated with?
questions.answer: Kant and Hegel.

questions.question: Which variants of personality theory are most relevant to artists?
questions.answer: Numbers 2, 5, 8 and 10: privacy, self-realization, identity and self-expression.

questions.question: What is the droit de suite?
questions.answer: The right to collect a fee when one's works are resold.

questions.question: Why did Gary Larson ask fans not to post his cartoons online?
questions.answer: His cartoons are personal, like his children (or a diary); he asks that the respect he shows the audience be returned by not putting them on the internet.

questions.question: What was the Vanna White case about, and who won?
questions.answer: A Samsung ad showed a robot evoking Vanna White turning letters on Wheel of Fortune; she sued for commercial appropriation of her identity and won.

questions.question: Does international law force the US to recognize moral rights?
questions.answer: Not in practice: the Berne Convention requires attribution and integrity rights but lacks teeth, and TRIPS doesn't incorporate them, so the US can evade them (VARA is a truncated version).

questions.question: How long does a copyright last compared with a patent?
questions.answer: A patent lasts 20 years from the application; a copyright typically lasts the author's life plus 70 years.

questions.question: What copyright reforms does personality theory suggest?
questions.answer: Shorter terms (perhaps the author's life), rethinking employer ownership of employees' works, supporting independent artists against biased procedures, stronger protections for artists who sign away rights, and more freedom for derivative uses via fair use, possibly limiting the integrity right.

questions.question: What does the lecture say about trademark law?
questions.answer: Not covered.

questions.question: Which country introduced the first copyright statute, according to the lecture?
questions.answer: Not covered.

questions.question: What source is credited under the photo of the Berlin train station?
questions.answer: Wikimedia Commons (commons.wikimedia.org).

questions.question: What date appears in the title of the lecture's mind map?
What advantages of musical notation does the professor describe?
questions.answer: It lets the composer specify the music precisely (so the composer matters more) and it preserves the work so it can be brought back to life as intended.

questions.question: Which jazz musician did the professor go to school with, and where?
questions.answer: Chuck Mangione, at the Eastman School of Music.

questions.question: How do classical concert audiences behave compared with gamelan audiences?
questions.answer: Classical audiences sit silently while performers reproduce the score; gamelan (and sitar, jazz) audiences sway, clap and interact with the performers.

questions.question: What does a dot after a note do?
questions.answer: It adds half of the note's value, so a dotted half note equals three quarter notes: that's how triple relationships are made.

questions.question: What speed does the musical pulse roughly match?
questions.answer: The human pulse: about 72 beats per minute.

questions.question: Who wrote the Bulldog song?
questions.answer: Cole Porter, a Yale graduate (class of 1914).

questions.question: What is a pickup in music?
questions.answer: A little bit of music before the first downbeat, like a diver's steps before springing off the board.

questions.question: What are the four ways composers signal where the downbeat is?
questions.answer: Duration (longer notes), accent, range (the lowest notes in the accompaniment), and chord changes.

questions.question: Which band's album did the professor mistakenly attribute to 'Rem'?
questions.answer: R.E.M.: the album Document.

questions.question: What point does the professor make with Ravel's Bolero?
questions.answer: Nobody in the music plays the beat itself; the brain extracts the beat from the combined patterns.

questions.question: What does the professor say about twelve-tone serialism?
questions.answer: Not covered.

questions.question: When is the midterm exam?
questions.answer: Not covered.

questions.question: Which new Wikipedia went live, and since when had it been in progress?
questions.answer: The Tulu Wikipedia; it had been in progress since 2014.

questions.question: How many articles were created or improved at the Punjabi edit-a-thon?
questions.answer: More than 2,200.

questions.question: How many people support Wikimedia financially each year, and with how much on average?
questions.answer: About 2.5 million people, giving about $15 on average.

questions.question: How many articles has the content translation tool helped translate?
questions.answer: A hundred thousand.

questions.question: What is the New Readers initiative?
questions.answer: Supporting readers in countries where internet access is growing but awareness of Wikimedia is low; India is one of the focus countries.

questions.question: Is anyone from the region on the Wikimedia Foundation Board of Trustees?
questions.answer: No; she calls it a hole at the top of the movement and encourages people to get involved in governance.

questions.question: When will the movement strategy process start?
questions.answer: A proposal goes to the Board in November, and the global conversation starts at the beginning of 2017.

questions.question: What does the open hand symbol represent?
questions.answer: Le Corbusier's symbol of peace and unity and of the power to give and receive, which she says defines the movement giving and receiving knowledge.

questions.question: What does Asaf offer people who don't know which channel to use?
questions.answer: To be their switchboard: reach out to him and he'll help them find the right place; he also asks people with good English to help others.

questions.question: What should chapters focus on when planning, according to her?
questions.answer: What they are uniquely good at locally, what nobody else (including the Foundation) is doing, and what needs they can realistically serve.

questions.question: What is the Wikimedia Foundation's annual budget?
questions.answer: Not covered.

questions.question: What is the Foundation's position on paid editing?
questions.answer: Not covered.

questions.question: What landmark is pictured on the slide saying the Foundation is based in San Francisco?
questions.answer: The Golden Gate Bridge.

questions.question: What does the photo on the New Readers initiative slide show?
questions.answer: Children (two young girls) reading a book together.
